chapters.title: Chapter 435: Haruna’s Silent Scars
paragraphs: Hannah turned back to face the front, her voice barely above a whisper. "Haruna, what was that? What just happened? It seemed like more than just cleaning a stain."
Haruna sighed, her voice soft and gentle. "It was nothing, Hannah. Just an accident. Jack was helping me clean the sauce. It’s not a big deal."
Hannah’s voice was filled with a mix of concern and curiosity. "But Haruna, it didn’t look like just an accident. It looked like there was something more going on. You can’t deny that."
Haruna’s eyes met Hannah’s briefly before looking down, her voice barely a whisper. "Okay, stop teasing me like that, Hannah. It’s not funny anymore."
Hannah’s expression softened, but her eyes still held a hint of curiosity. "I’m not teasing you, Haruna. I’m just concerned. You seemed really affected by what happened."

I noticed Julie also kept looking at the rearview mirror, her eyes flickering between the road and us. The car ride continued, and after an hour’s drive, Haruna and Hannah kept chatting, their excitement about going to America palpable.
I looked at Haruna and asked, "Haruna, who else is in your family? I’d like to know more about you."

Haruna’s expression softened as she thought about her family. "I have my elder sister who lives here with me, and my mom is in Japan. We tried to bring her with us, but she didn’t want to come with us."
I asked, "Why is that? Did something happen?"

Haruna’s voice was tinged with sadness. "It’s because my dad bought that house, and we grew up there. But after my dad passed away in an accident, my mom didn’t want to leave that house alone without anyone to take care of it. She is a traditional Japanese mom. No matter how many times my sister and I convinced her, she didn’t listen to us."
I said hurriedly, "I am sorry, Haruna. I didn’t know. I didn’t mean to bring up those sad memories. I am really sorry if I upset you."
Haruna’s voice was gentle but filled with a deep sorrow. "No, it’s okay, Jack. Really, I am used to it. It’s just something I have to live with."

I saw a bit of tears in her eyes, and I hugged her tightly, comforting her and whispering in her ear, "How can you be okay, Haruna? You don’t have to be so tough on yourself. You are not alone in this. You have Hannah, and your sister, and I am also here for you, okay? We are friends, and we care about you."

Haruna’s body trembled slightly as she hugged me back, her tears soaking into my shirt. She felt a mix of emotions, her heart heavy with grief but also filled with a sense of warmth and comfort from my words. "Thank you, Jack. That really means a lot to me. I just... I miss him so much, you know? Some days are harder than others."

I held her close, my hand gently rubbing her back in a soothing motion. "It’s okay to miss him, Haruna. It’s okay to feel sad. You don’t have to put on a brave face all the time. We’re here for you, and we want to support you."
Haruna nodded slightly, her grip on me tightening just a fraction. "I know, Jack. Thank you for understanding. It’s just hard sometimes, you know? To keep going when a part of you is missing."

I continued to hold her, my voice steady and reassuring. "I can’t imagine how hard it must be, Haruna. But you have people who care about you, and we want to help you through this. You don’t have to go through it alone."

Haruna’s voice was muffled against my shoulder, her words barely audible. "Thank you, Jack. That means more to me than you know. I just... I need to be strong for my mom and my sister, you know? They need me."
I nodded, my hand still gently rubbing her back in a soothing motion. "You are strong, Haruna. But even the strongest people need support sometimes. And that’s what we’re here for."
Haruna took a deep, shuddering breath, her grip on me loosening slightly as she tried to compose herself. "I know, Jack. It’s just hard sometimes. But I’ll be okay. I have to be."

I could feel the weight of her emotions, the way her body trembled slightly as she tried to hold back more tears. "It’s okay to not be okay, Haruna. We all have moments like this. It’s part of being human."
Haruna nodded, her voice steady but filled with a deep sadness. "I know. It’s just... It’s hard to let go sometimes. But I’ll try. For my mom and sister, I’ll try to be strong."

I held her for a moment longer, giving her the time she needed to gather herself. When she finally pulled away, her eyes were still glistening with unshed tears, but there was a hint of determination in them.

I gently wiped away her tears with my thumb, offering her a small, reassuring smile. "You’re doing great, Haruna," I whispered softly, my voice filled with warmth and understanding. "It’s okay to feel this way. We all need time to heal."

Julie, who had been quietly driving, glanced at Haruna through the rearview mirror, her eyes filled with compassion. "Haruna, dear," she said, her voice gentle and soothing, "it’s okay to feel this way. We all have our moments. Remember, it’s okay to lean on others when you need to."
Haruna nodded, her voice steady but tinged with emotion. "I know. Thank you, Aunt Julie. It means a lot to me."
I noticed Hannah looking at me with a sad look in her eyes.[Jack has also been through that... when his mom and dad passed away... he must also have been sad... even now...]

Hannah’s thoughts were filled with empathy and a deep understanding of the pain we both carried. She reached out, placing a gentle hand on Haruna’s arm, her touch warm and comforting. "We’re here for you, Haruna. Both of us. You don’t have to go through this alone."
Haruna looked at Hannah, her eyes filled with gratitude and a hint of a smile. "Thank you, Hannah. That means a lot to me. I know I can be a bit much sometimes, but I really appreciate you both."
Hannah smiled softly, her eyes meeting Haruna’s with a sense of solidarity. "You’re not too much, Haruna. We care about you. And we want to help you through this."
Julie added, her voice warm and comforting, "You’re part of our family, Haruna. We’re here to support you, always."

Haruna took a deep breath, her eyes slowly clearing as she gathered her strength. The car ride was filled with a mix of emotions, but there was also a sense of comfort and support. We all shared a bond, a connection that went beyond words.

chapters.title: Chapter 436: Hannah’s Misstep
paragraphs: As we drove, the scenery outside began to change, the landscape becoming more picturesque. The rolling hills stretched out before us, their green slopes dotted with wildflowers and ancient trees.

The sky above was a canvas of dark, brooding clouds, their edges tinged with silver as the sun struggled to break through. The air was filled with a sense of anticipation, the beauty of nature unfolding before our eyes.
Soon, we reached the Neuschwanstein Castle. The scene outside was breathtaking, the castle standing tall and proud against the backdrop of the dramatic sky.

Its towers reached towards the heavens, their stone facades weathered by time but still majestic. The castle was perched on a rugged hill, surrounded by lush forests and the rolling hills that seemed to cradle it protectively.

Haruna looked out of the window, her eyes widening at the sight. "It’s beautiful," she whispered, her voice filled with awe and wonder. The castle’s intricate architecture, with its turrets and battlements, seemed to tell a story of a bygone era, a tale of knights and royalty.

Hannah, with her auburn hair and sparkling green eyes, had been particularly excited about visiting the castle. Her youthful energy was infectious, and even Julie, who was usually more reserved, couldn’t help but smile at her daughter’s enthusiasm.

As we stepped out of the car, the cool breeze greeted us, carrying with it the scent of pine and earth. The castle loomed before us, even more impressive up close than it had been from a distance. Its stone walls were adorned with ivy, adding a touch of nature’s green to the man-made structure.

The windows, tall and arched, reflected the surrounding landscape, blurring the lines between the castle and its environment. The grandeur of the place seemed to cast a spell over us, making everything feel a bit more magical.
Hannah smiled, her eyes sparkling with excitement. "It really is," she said, her voice filled with awe. "I can’t wait to explore it. It’s like something out of a fairy tale."

Julie parked the car, and we all stepped out. The cool breeze greeted us as we stood there, taking in the view. The castle was even more impressive up close, its intricate details and grand scale leaving us all in awe.

As we walked towards the entrance, Haruna’s steps were lighter, her earlier sadness replaced with a sense of wonder and curiosity. "I can’t believe we’re actually here," she said, her voice filled with excitement and a childlike wonder. The castle seemed to have a calming effect on her, lifting her spirits and making her forget her earlier worries.

I smiled, feeling a sense of contentment and joy at seeing Haruna’s spirits lifted. "It’s going to be a great day," I said, my voice steady and reassuring. "We’ll make sure of it." I could feel the excitement building within me as well, the anticipation of exploring the castle and discovering its secrets.

Julie took us around, walking towards the castle with a sense of purpose. I took pictures of her, capturing the moment as she looked around, her eyes wide with wonder. The way the sunlight filtered through the trees and cast dappled shadows on the ground created a beautiful pattern that seemed to dance around us.

As I looked around, I felt like this place was a bit romantic, the castle’s grandeur and the surrounding landscape creating a sense of magic and enchantment. It was as if we had stepped into another world, one where anything was possible.

We climbed to the top of the castle to see the scenery, the stone steps worn smooth by the passage of time. The view from the top was breathtaking, the landscape stretching out before us in a patchwork of green and gold. The castle, with its towering walls and ancient stones, stood as a testament to the past, a silent witness to the history that had unfolded within its walls.

As Hannah was climbing the stairs, she slipped on a loose stone, her foot twisting awkwardly beneath her. She let out a cry of pain as she fell back, her body tumbling down the steps. The sound of her fall seemed to echo through the castle, a sharp contrast to the serene beauty around us.

I was behind her, and I caught her, my arms wrapping around her waist, pulling her close to me. "Be careful, okay?" I said, my voice filled with concern, my body pressed against hers, my arms holding her tightly, my breath hot against her neck. The feel of her body against mine sent a jolt of electricity through me, a mix of concern and something more primal.

Hannah blushed, her face turning a shade of pink, her body trembling slightly in my arms. "Hmm... thank you," she said, her voice soft and filled with gratitude, her body pressing against mine, her breath hitching slightly. The warmth of her body seeped into me, and I could feel her heart beating rapidly, a stark contrast to the stillness of the castle around us.

Julie rushed to her side, her eyes wide with concern and worry. "Hannah, are you okay?" she asked, her voice filled with panic and fear, her hands reaching out to touch her daughter, her fingers trembling slightly. Her maternal instinct was palpable, and her concern for Hannah overrode everything else. She knelt beside her daughter, her hands gently probing the injured ankle, her touch soft and careful.

Hannah winced, her face contorting with pain. "I... I must have sprained my ankle..." she said, her voice filled with discomfort and distress, her body trembling slightly, her breath coming in ragged gasps. The pain seemed to radiate from her, a tangible force that made the air around us feel heavy and tense.

I let Hannah sit on the stairs, my arms still wrapped around her, my body pressed against hers, my breath hot against her neck. I could feel her body trembling slightly, her breath coming in ragged gasps, her body pressing against mine, her heat seeping into me, her scent filling my nostrils, a mix of her perfume and her natural aroma, a musky, intoxicating fragrance that sent waves of desire through me. The closeness of our bodies created an intimate space, a bubble where only we existed, the rest of the world fading away.

Julie’s face paled, her eyes filled with worry and concern. "Let me see," she said, her voice filled with urgency and care, her hands gently touching her daughter’s ankle, her fingers probing the injury, her touch soft and gentle.

She examined the ankle with a practiced eye, her fingers moving carefully over the skin, checking for any signs of serious injury. The way she handled the situation was a testament to her strength and love for her daughter.

The swelling was evident, a visible sign of the pain Hannah was trying so hard to hide. Julie’s concern was a tangible force, her love for her daughter evident in every touch and glance.

The way Julie looked at me, her eyes filled with gratitude and relief, made me feel a sense of purpose, a desire to protect and care for those I loved.

The way she looked at me, the trust and gratitude in her eyes, made me feel a deep connection to her, a bond that went beyond words.

I stopped her before she could say anything further, my voice firm yet gentle. The golden light of the setting sun cast a warm glow on her face, highlighting the tears that still glistened in her eyes.

Hannah had a sad look on her face, her eyes filled with discomfort and distress. "You guys go up, and I will wait for you here, okay..." she said, her voice soft and filled with sadness, her body trembling slightly, her breath coming in ragged gasps. The way she tried to push us away, to make us continue without her, was a testament to her selflessness, her desire not to ruin the day for everyone else.

I knelt down beside her, my eyes level with hers, my voice soft and comforting. "Hannah, we’re not leaving you here alone. We’re a team, and we stick together," I said, my hand gently squeezing hers, my touch soft and reassuring. The golden light of the setting sun seemed to wrap around us, creating a halo of warmth and comfort that made everything feel a bit more bearable.

Julie, her eyes filled with concern and love, knelt down beside Hannah as well, her hand gently stroking her daughter’s hair. "We’re not going anywhere without you, sweetheart," she said, her voice soft and gentle, her touch soothing and caring. The way she looked at Hannah, the love and concern in her eyes, was a beautiful sight, a testament to the bond they shared.
I looked into her eyes, my voice soft and gentle. "How can we let you miss such beautiful scenery? You are coming with us..."

Hannah’s eyes filled with a hint of sadness, a stark contrast to the golden hues around us. "How can I... I can’t even walk," she said, her voice soft and filled with despair. A single tear rolled down her cheek, glinting in the sunlight. Her body trembled slightly as she looked at her injured ankle, the pain and discomfort evident in her eyes.

I took out my handkerchief and asked Julie to pour water on it to make it wet. Julie nodded, her eyes filled with concern and care, and she carefully poured water on the handkerchief, her hands trembling slightly as she did so.

The cool water dripped onto the fabric, making it glisten in the fading light. I gently bound the wet handkerchief to Hannah’s ankle, the coldness of the water making her gasp as it helped relieve the pain.
I asked, "Do you feel any better?"

She nodded, a soft "Hmm" escaping her lips, her eyes filled with gratitude and relief. "Thank you," she said, her voice soft and filled with appreciation. Her body relaxed slightly as the coldness of the water seemed to ease her pain, but her eyes still held a deep sadness.

As I looked at her, I could see the thoughts running through her mind, the mix of emotions in her eyes.[Jack is so caring... how good it would be if he really were my boyfriend... but Mom...]she thought, her eyes flickering with a mix of longing and sadness. The golden light of the setting sun seemed to highlight the tears in her eyes, making them glisten like precious gems.

"Aah... don’t..." she said, her voice soft and filled with surprise. Her body trembled slightly in my arms, her breath coming in ragged gasps, her eyes wide with disbelief and wonder.

The way she looked at me, the mix of emotions in her eyes, made me feel a deep sense of fulfillment. The golden light of the setting sun seemed to wrap around us, creating a halo of warmth and comfort.

As I carried her, other tourists also paid attention to the scene. They whispered among themselves, their eyes filled with admiration and envy. "Look at them... they look so perfect together," one tourist said, her voice filled with longing. "The boy is so caring. I wish I had someone like that," another added, her eyes locked onto us, her voice soft and dreamy.
"Such a lovely couple," an older woman commented, her voice warm and approving. "He carries her like she’s a princess. True love is rare to see."

Hannah blushed deeply, her face turning a deeper shade of red. She buried her face in my shoulder, her body trembling slightly in my arms. The whispers of the tourists created a soft hum in the air, a symphony of admiration and envy that seemed to blend with the golden light of the setting sun.

Haruna teased Hannah, her eyes filled with amusement and mischief. "Hannah, your boyfriend is so good to you..." she said, her voice soft and playful. Her eyes sparkled with joy as she looked at us, her smile wide and teasing.

Hannah’s blush deepened, her face turning an even deeper shade of red. "H-He’s not my boyfriend," she stammered, her voice soft and filled with embarrassment. Her eyes locked onto Haruna, her body still pressed against mine, her arms wrapped around my neck, her breath coming in ragged gasps. The golden light of the setting sun seemed to dance around us, creating a magical atmosphere that made everything feel even more enchanting.

chapters.title: Chapter 438: Hannah’s Feelings
paragraphs: As we slowly climbed to the top of the castle, Hannah in my arms, I could feel her heartbeat quicken, her breath warm against my neck. The physical exertion of carrying her up the stairs made me sweat, but the emotional weight of her closeness was even more intense.
Her thoughts were a whirlwind of emotions, a mix of admiration, conflict, and something deeper, something she couldn’t quite name.

[Jack is so strong,] she thought, her mind racing. [He’s carrying me and climbing up... I can feel his heartbeat, and his face and lips are so close...] The warmth of his body against hers, the rhythm of their breaths syncing, created an intimate connection that was hard to ignore. She could feel the muscles in his arms flexing as he carried her, the strength and warmth of his body making her feel safe and protected.
[He’s sweating... Mom is so lucky to have Jack, who loves her...]she continued, her thoughts drifting to Julie and the bond she shared with me.
But then, a pang of guilt and confusion hit her.[No... I shouldn’t think like that... What about Dad? He will be sad and angry if he finds out Mom has betrayed and cheated on him with Jack...]

Her internal conflict deepened, her thoughts tangled in a web of emotions.[And I am here to let Jack fall in love with me... not letting them be together... Hannah, focus! You can’t think like that...]she admonished herself, trying to push away the thoughts that made her feel guilty and conflicted. But despite her efforts, the thoughts kept coming, the feelings kept growing.
As we climbed, Julie turned to me, her eyes filled with concern and gratitude. "Let me wipe it for you..." she said softly, her hand gently wiping the sweat from my face with her handkerchief.
The touch was tender and caring, a small act that spoke volumes about her feelings. She then handed me a water bottle, her eyes never leaving mine, a silent thank you for taking care of her daughter.

I took a sip of the water, feeling the cool liquid soothe my parched throat. "It’s okay... we are almost there..." I said, my voice steady despite the physical strain. The weight of Hannah in my arms was nothing compared to the emotional weight of the moment, the bond we all shared in that instant.

We soon reached the top of the castle, the view stretching out before us in a breathtaking panorama. The golden light of the setting sun bathed the landscape, casting long shadows and highlighting the beauty of the scene.

Hannah was still in my arms, her breath hitting my neck, her chest slightly pressing against mine. The warmth of her body, the closeness of our breaths, created an intimate moment that was both comforting and charged with unspoken emotions.

Hannah blushed, her face turning a shade of pink. "You... can put me down now..." she said, her voice soft and filled with a mix of embarrassment and gratitude. The way she looked at me, the mix of emotions in her eyes, made me feel a deep sense of connection to her, a bond that went beyond words.

I gently put her down, but as soon as her foot touched the ground, she winced in pain. "Ah..." she gasped, her body trembling slightly, her breath coming in ragged gasps. The pain seemed to radiate from her, a tangible force that made the air around us feel heavy and tense.

I quickly supported her, my arms wrapping around her, my body pressing against hers, my breath hot against her neck. "Don’t be brave, what if you hurt it even further..." I said, my voice filled with concern and care. The way she looked at me, the mix of emotions in her eyes, made me feel a deep sense of protectiveness, a desire to shield her from any more pain.

I looked at Julie and Haruna, my eyes filled with determination and reassurance. "You guys stay here... I will go to the medical shop to get something to relieve the pain... okay..." I said, my voice steady and comforting. The way they looked at me, the trust and gratitude in their eyes, made me feel a deep sense of purpose, a desire to take care of them, to make them feel safe and protected.
Hannah’s eyes filled with a mix of emotions, her body trembling slightly as she tried to protest. "No... I am really fine... I..." she started, but I didn’t let her finish.

I quickly made my way to a corner where no one was, the urgency of the moment driving me forward. I bought a normal syrup from theSUDIXsystem store, a small act that I hoped would bring her some relief.

I also dripped a few drops of my blood into the syrup, a secret ingredient that I knew would help heal her instantly. I also bought a pain-relieving patch from theSUDIX store, just for the show, a small act that I hoped would bring her some comfort.

As I made my way back to them, the syrup and patch in hand, I couldn’t help but feel a sense of happiness and fulfillment. The castle seemed to stand as a testament to the moment, its ancient walls and grandeur creating a sense of magic and enchantment, a stark contrast to the earlier pain and discomfort, a testament to the joy and comfort that we felt in the moment.

Hannah’s thoughts were still a whirlwind, her emotions a tangled web of feelings. She looked at me, her eyes filled with a mix of admiration, conflict, and something deeper that she couldn’t quite name. "Why does he have to be so kind? It’s like he can see right through me," she thought.

When she looked at Haruna, her best friend, she felt a pang of jealousy, an emotion she had never experienced before.[Haruna always seems so confident around him. Why can’t I be like that?]she wondered.
Glancing at Julie, her mom, she felt a twinge of guilt, another feeling she had never wanted to feel.[Mom has always been there for me, and here I am, feeling things I shouldn’t,]she thought.

As I handed her the syrup, our fingers brushed, and she felt a jolt of electricity that made her heart race and her breath hitch.[His touch sends shivers down my spine. What is happening to me?]Hannah thought. "Here, drink this first. It will help you recover," I said gently.
